title: The Hollow Hollow
premise: When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, Xanthe Voss learns their late mistress was the last Keeper of a covenant binding the mortal realm to the fae Otherworld—and that Xanthe's own blood is the missing seal. Hunted by the usurper Aldric Vane's witch-finders and distrusted by the fae court they must petition, Xanthe gathers a ragged company of outlaws, exiled nobles, and half-fae smugglers to reach the Hollow Hollow, the dead heart of the old covenant. There they discover Vane seeks not conquest but godhood through the stolen starlight, and that restoring the covenant demands a living anchor willing to be unmade. In the end, Xanthe refuses both sacrifice and surrender, instead rewriting the covenant so it binds no one alone—sharing the anchor among all who swore it—and the stars return over free cities that will never again outlaw what keeps them alive.
about_author: Juniper Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal fishing villages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about outsiders who build families from fragments, and they still cannot resist collecting superstitions.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Selling luck-knots in the occupied city of Greyharbor, Xanthe hides their magic behind mundane craft while witch-finders sweep the market. A child pays with a coin stamped with the old covenant sigil—Xanthe's own family mark. Emotional beat: the ache of hiding who you are.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The border wards shatter at moonrise and every star gutters out; the city erupts in panic as fae light bleeds through the cracks. Xanthe's hidden magic flares visibly for the first time in five years. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined—the mask is gone.

chapters.title: What the Mistress Left
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, fleeing to their buried cache, finds a letter from their dead mistress revealing she was the last Keeper and that Xanthe's blood can reforge the broken covenant—if they reach the Hollow Hollow before the next dark moon. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Witch-Finders at the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Captain Sera Dune, a witch-finder who begins doubting her orders when she's told to burn children. She lets Xanthe slip her net, an act of quiet treason. Emotional beat: the first crack in loyalty to an unjust law.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Half-fae smuggler Bramble Ferrow agrees to guide Xanthe toward the free cities—for a price: Xanthe's promise to restore the crossings her fae kin are trapped behind. Emotional beat: wary bargain, the first thread of belonging.

chapters.title: Free Cities, Chained Hearts
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the free city of Vellamere, Xanthe petitions the Council of Nine, who fear open war more than tyranny and refuse aid. An exiled noble, Lord Cassian Roe, offers his private army instead—at a cost Xanthe doesn't yet understand. Emotional beat: disillusionment with institutions.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: Aldric Vane's POV. Vane drinks distilled starlight and grows stranger, hungrier; he orders the free cities besieged and dispatches his Inquisitor General to capture 'the Voss girl or boy or whatever it is.' Emotional beat: cold ambition masking a hollow core.

chapters.title: Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Company POV (rotating). The company crosses a burned borderland where refugees mistake Xanthe for a saint because of their glowing blood. Xanthe, uncomfortable with worship, teaches them practical wards instead. Emotional beat: identity as something given by community, not claimed alone.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Ordered to execute a village of charm-sellers, Sera defects outright, killing her superior and fleeing with evidence of Vane's star-harvesting camps. She intercepts Xanthe's company on the road. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: The Crossing That Shouldn't Open
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Guided by Bramble's fading fae-sight, the company slips through a wild crossing into the Otherworld's edge—beautiful, lethal, and starving since the stars went out. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by wrongness.

chapters.title: Court of Thorns and Hunger
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The fae court receives them with contempt: mortals broke the covenant first, they claim, and they demand Xanthe's blood as payment regardless. Cassian secretly negotiates a side deal. Emotional beat: betrayal within the found family's fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Cassian's Price
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. His deal revealed: he wants the covenant rewritten to restore his family's stolen throne, using Xanthe as a figurehead. Xanthe refuses to be anyone's symbol; the company fractures. Emotional beat: the difference between belonging and being used.

chapters.title: The Hollow Hollow
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They reach the covenant's dead heart—a vast hollow tree where the first oath was sworn—and learn the truth: the Keepers didn't guard the covenant, they were its anchors, consumed one by one. Emotional beat: horror and clarity; the true cost revealed.

chapters.title: Vane Ascendant
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. At the siege of Vellamere, Vane consumes enough hoarded starlight to become something barely human, and the sky above the free cities goes utterly black. Emotional beat: dread; the antagonist transcends politics into apocalypse.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Company POV (rotating). Around a dying campfire, each member confesses why they came—and Xanthe realizes the covenant was never meant for one Keeper but for many hands. The idea of a shared anchor takes root. Emotional beat: hope forged from honesty.

chapters.title: The Dark Moon March
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Racing Vane's vanguard to the Hollow Hollow, the company fights a night battle at the ford of Mirren with refugee militias Sera once would have burned. Emotional beat: former instruments of the law fighting beside the outlawed.

chapters.title: Blood and Bargain
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the hollow tree, Xanthe offers their blood—but the fae queen arrives demanding sole custody of the new covenant, and Vane crashes the rite seeking to devour the anchor itself. Three-way standoff at the world's hinge. Emotional beat: everything converges, nothing resolved.

chapters.title: The Unmaking Offered
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The rite shows Xanthe the anchor's fate: dissolution into the covenant's fabric, self erased. Alone, they almost accept it—until every member of the company steps into the circle unbidden, each offering a piece of themselves. Emotional beat: love answering despair.

chapters.title: A Covenant of Many Hands
chapters.summary: Company POV (rapid rotation). Together they rewrite the oath—no single anchor, but a web of willing keepers across both realms—and channel it against Vane, who shatters as the stolen starlight tears free of him. Emotional beat: triumph earned collectively, not heroically alone.

chapters.title: Stars Over Greyharbor
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The stars return; the crossings reopen; Bramble's kin come home weeping. But the free cities' councils, terrified of the new visible magic, move to regulate it—and Xanthe stands before them as witness, not petitioner. Emotional beat: victory complicated by the old habits of power.

chapters.title: The Charter of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera presents her evidence of Vane's crimes to a reckoning tribunal; the witch-finder order is dissolved and rebuilt as wardens bound by consent, not decree. Xanthe's charter—magic taught openly, kept by communities—is ratified in Greyharbor where they were once hunted. Emotional beat: justice institutionalized without losing its soul.

chapters.title: Keeper, Unalone
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, epilogue. A year later, Xanthe teaches apprentices in a rebuilt hedge-school, visits the hollow tree now green again, and finally signs their full name to a spell—first time ever. Belonging, they understand, was never granted; it was built. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
